title: Kamakura shogunate
summary: Minamoto no Yoritomo defeated the Taira clan at Dannoura in 1185 and founded Japan's first military government, the shogunate, based at Kamakura while the imperial court stayed in Kyoto. After his death the Hojo family ruled as shogunal regents, holding the real power behind puppet shoguns. The regime survived the Mongol invasions of 1274 and 1281 and fell in 1333, when the Ashikaga took over as shoguns. It opened a medieval age of warrior government that lasted until 1573.

uncertainty.note: Dating start from Yoritomo's victory at Dan-no-ura and establishment of the shugo/jito administrative system in 1185; some accounts date the formal shogunate from his appointment as seii taishogun in 1192. End is 1333 when imperial forces overthrew the bakufu.

as_recorded.value: The Kamakura Period or Kamakura Jidai (1185-1333 CE)
founded Japan's first military government, or shogunate, in 1185

where.modern_name: Kamakura, Kanagawa Prefecture, Japan (administrative seat of the shogunate)

importance.justification: Founded the warrior government that shaped Japan for centuries, down to the Tokugawa shogunate (R2 D3 T3 L3).

related.because: The Kamakura shogunate organized and funded the samurai coastal defense of Hakata Bay against Kublai Khan's invasions.
The Kamakura bakufu founded the institutional framework of warrior governance that culminated centuries later in the Tokugawa shogunate.
